ctor.rationale: `base(0, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.AllEnemies)` with `protected override bool HasEnergyCostX => true` (Whirlwind.cs:22-29) == `energy_cost_x = True` (cards/base.py:84-87), `_energy_cost = 0`, ATTACK / UNCOMMON / ALL_ENEMIES. The base cost of 0 is exactly right for an X-cost card: `CardEnergyCost`'s constructor sets `Canonical = ((!CostsX) ? canonicalCost : 0)` (CardEnergyCost.cs:86). `handles_own_routing = True` is faithful for the same reason as card/conflagration's: C#'s OnPlay runs once and the multi-hit fan-out happens inside the attack command.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(5m, ValueProp.Move)` (Whirlwind.cs:24) == `_damage = 5` per hit, powered on both sides.

OnPlay.issue: The X-value plumbing, the hit count and the hits-outer/enemies-inner loop order are all faithful: `WithHitCount(ResolveEnergyXValue())` on `TargetingAllOpponents(CombatState)` (Whirlwind.cs:33, 42-45) == `for _ in range(self.captured_x)` with a per-hit living-enemy sweep, where `captured_x` is set by the play pipeline as `hooks.modify_x_value(card, player.energy)` (combat.py:547-549), the sim's ResolveEnergyXValue. AttackCommand re-derives `validTargets` from `where c.IsAlive` at the top of each hit (AttackCommand.cs:544-546), which the sim's per-hit `[e for e in ctx.enemies if not e.is_gone]` matches, and both break when none remain. ALL-ENEMIES FAN-OUT: C# passes the whole valid-target list to ONE `CreatureCmd.Damage(targets: validTargets)` call per hit (AttackCommand.cs:650), computing every DamageResult before any `Kill` (CreatureCmd.cs:372-409); the sim issues a separate `DamageCmd.deal` per enemy, so each death resolves before the next enemy is damaged. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/conflagration's OnPlay entry (rule 3). DORMANT -- no ported Ironclad-reachable monster has an on-death effect that changes a sibling's incoming damage. Presentation, folded in: the whole `if (num > 0)` VFX block (34-41), which draws horizontal lines and a vignette scaled by the FastMode player setting and plays a sound; it touches no state, and note that the sim needs no `num > 0` guard because a zero-iteration loop does nothing.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(3m)` (Whirlwind.cs:50) == `self._damage += 3` (5 -> 8 per hit). The hit count stays X on both sides.
